objects: Two regions x and y that share only a boundary point.
x and y are two disks intersecting at a single point on their boundaries.
Let x and y be two regions where x is a proper part of y (P(x,y) is true). Then, x and y must share points, so DC(x,y) is false.
x and y are two regions where x is a proper part of y and they touch at a single point on their boundaries.
x and y are two disjoint regions.
x and y where TPP(x,y) is true, but Pi(x,y) is false.
x and y where NTPP(x,y) holds, but C(x,y) is false.
Let x be a large region and y be a smaller region entirely contained within x. Then Pi(x,y) is true, but P(x,y) is false.
Let x be a square and y be a smaller square entirely contained within x. Then PPi(x,y) is true, but P(x,y) is false.
x and y where y is a tangential proper part of x.
x and y where y is a tangential proper part of x but x is not a proper part of y.
x and y are two regions where y is a tangential proper part of x and they are connected.
x and y are two regions where x is a proper part of y, they overlap, but their boundaries do not touch.
x and y are two overlapping regions where y is a proper part of x.
x and y are equal regions.
Let x be a square and y be a smaller square strictly inside x. Then O(x,y) and PPi(x,y) are true, but EQ(x,y) is false.
x is a smaller region entirely contained within y, sharing some interior points and touching at the boundary.
x and y are two regions that are partially overlapped and connected, but x is not a part of y.
x and y are two circles where y is entirely contained within x, they overlap, are connected, partially overlapped, and y is a proper part of x, but their boundaries do not touch.
x and y are identical regions.
